A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VITA and retain the same research framework and Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison, including material that was renamed, redrawn, or relocated.

before.justification: V2 reports original BridgeData generalization and expert-versus-scripted evaluations, Meta-World offline-RL results, and sampling and adaptation ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds recurrent-baseline results, an explicit-memory control, cloth-manipulation evaluations, and numerical hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: VITA retains its frozen CLIP encoder, concatenated representations, adaptation MLP, regression head, meta-learned reconstruction objective, sequential updates, and dissimilarity-based sampling. CLIP-GRU and TTT-EX are comparison variants, not new components of VITA. Expanded descriptions do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds sc_pnp_cloth, illustrated with the instruction 'Move the cloth,' to the scripted discrimination evaluation and sampling ablation. This extends the represented manipulation cases beyond objects, rigid items, soft toys, and utensils. Training coverage, the ten generalization subsets, and Meta-World MT10 remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V4 adds CLIP-GRU to all three principal comparisons in Tables 1–2, providing a consequential learned temporal baseline absent from v2. Appendix F.2 also adds TTT-EX. Existing evaluated comparators remain; TTT-OF becomes TTT-TR, while the memoryless TTT-VIS is called TTT-RS in the prose.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 expands the reported learning-rate grid with 0.05 and 0.001. The new TTT-EX control uses an eight-frame window and selects learning rate 1.0 with one update. D.3 replaces v2's ambiguous VITA rates '0.1 and 1.0' with 0.1; this documents a revision without establishing reruns. Principal splits, metrics, and offline-RL budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 substantially supplements the temporal-adaptation analysis: new Table 4 reports learning-rate/step sensitivity, and Appendix F.2 tests whether reset-based adaptation over recent frames can substitute for accumulated parameter memory. The sampling ablation also extends to cloth manipulation. These add evidence about sensitivity and the proposed memory mechanism beyond v2's reported analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report offline-RL experiments across ten random seeds, IQM aggregation, and 95% task-stratified bootstrap intervals using 10,000 resamples. CLIP-GRU receives the same uncertainty reporting. No additional statistical procedure or increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: New CLIP-GRU results exceed VITA on four of ten generalization datasets, including rd_fold: 0.726 versus 0.606. CLIP-GRU also records BinVOC 0.80 and MT10 IQM 0.777; retained VITA scores are unchanged. Expanding scripted coverage changes VLM-CL/CLIP-FT BinVOC averages from 0.25/0.75 to 0.40/0.80, which are not same-coverage gains. Sensitivity and TTT-EX results are newly reported.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the declared dimensions of PK, PV, and PQ from d′×d to d′×2d, making their products compatible with the already defined concatenated 2d-dimensional input. The assumptions, update equations, sampling objective, and Appendix G complexity derivation otherwise remain unchanged; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain their meaning. Section 6.1 adds a concluding claim that implicit memory generalizes more effectively than recurrent hidden-state memory, supported by the new CLIP-GRU discrimination and offline-RL comparisons. This is a limited extension of the central claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations connecting GRU failures to temporal shortcuts and explaining how window-averaged adaptation discards order or could double-count observations without resets. Appendix D.2 explains choosing one larger update over several smaller updates. Closed-loop control and complex RL are explicitly identified as future work; existing variability, duration, and deployment-safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 documents CLIP-GRU's shared encoder/head and single-layer, 64-unit GRU, plus TTT-EX's windowed gradient averaging and selected settings. However, Appendix D.2 removes v2's statement that adaptation parameters are not reset between evaluation episodes, leaving that boundary less explicit without establishing a changed reset policy. Most implementation and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: V4 adds the Cho et al. GRU and Vaswani et al. Transformer references. Section 2.2 explicitly positions parameter-based temporal memory against recurrent hidden states and cached key–value pairs. The previous references and broader related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in temporal-memory explanations, baseline interpretation, and Appendices D and F. Section 6 gains numbered discussion and limitations/future-work subsections; acknowledgments and a corresponding-author footnote are added. The overall narrative and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn to expose training/inference modules and supervision flow, and a new Figure 2 diagrams the detailed adaptation computation. V4 also adds the sensitivity table, expands comparison and ablation tables, and adds a cloth panel to the scripted examples. These materially revise visual explanation and displays beyond renumbering or numerical edits.

improvement.justification: The recurrent comparator missing from v2 makes v4's temporal-modeling claims more assessable and reveals meaningful limits: CLIP-GRU wins four generalization comparisons. The explicit-memory control, sensitivity results, and clearer diagrams further strengthen evidence and explanation. These gains are partly offset by removal of the between-episode reset disclosure and inconsistent TTT-RS/TTT-VIS naming, leaving a useful but bounded overall improvement.
